scope: Bounded packaged ARM64 Linux X11 GUI WebRTC workflows and a thirty-minute same-machine receiver run. No production changes authored in this work; newer upstream changes have separate package coverage. No full platform/performance qualification.

endurancePackage.note: Built from the recorded base revision plus changes captured exactly in the source archive. Later documentation/evidence files do not alter production sources.

upstreamIntegration.change: Preserved upstream trace/evidence work and the Wayland cursor exclusion change in window_capture.cpp. The latter is the only production change after the endurance package.
upstreamIntegration.coverage: Rebuilt and packaged the integrated ARM64 app, then repeated bounded GUI WebRTC workflows on Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 userlands. Thirty-minute endurance applies to the earlier exact artifact; native Wayland remains unqualified here.

environments: Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 owned userland on the same Jetson CPU/kernel
runtimeScope: Owned Xvfb/xfwm4 desktop, isolated session bus and GNOME keyring, private PulseAudio null sinks and remapped microphone. Native ARM browser and publisher on the same Jetson, using public VDO.Ninja signaling. No physical desktop or WAN/outage qualification.
changes: Reuse linux-arm64-bringup.py and the shared browser video/audio observer; optional WebRTC mode keeps the default UDP workflow.

Native browser records decoded video identities, stereo tone separation, microphone mix/mute, receiver connection, statistics and screenshots; its private output sink prevents feedback into captured audio.
Optional sustained reception records app RSS/anonymous memory, receiver progress, periodic decoded content/audio, then real GUI Stop/restart and saved-settings idle relaunch/Quit.
Close receiver/browser on normal EOF and signals; read saved fixture passwords through their GUI Show control.

gates.classification: native ARM64 build gate, not application testing
package construction and native ABI/provenance gates, not application testing

endurance.sampling: Statistics about every five seconds, with a four-second video plus three-second audio observation followed by a sixty-second pause between content observations. Browser presentation progress watched continuously.

preservedAttempts.explanation: Media, 67-second pilot and restart passed. The password assertion read protected accessibility bullets; the saved fixture password was present. Fixed by exercising the real Show control before reading and hiding afterward.
The isolated Ubuntu 24.04 browser could not load libnspr4.so. Added official Ubuntu libnspr4/libnss3 files only to the owned rootfs; no host libraries changed.

All five received-media phases, app Stop/Quit and saved-settings relaunch passed. The browser closed but its Node helper retained stdin. Fixed by closing the controller pipe after the close acknowledgement.

Stopped the first endurance setup after its initial mixed-media phase, before the timed endurance section, to fix the known helper EOF issue. SIGINT triggered owned-process cleanup; abrupt app termination left its report-local discovery file. This is not a completed endurance run.

remaining: Calibrated A/V synchronization/drift, continuous per-frame identity/cadence qualification, high-motion and higher profiles remain unqualified. Constant tones and periodic four-second video samples cannot establish those results.

The viewer reconnection closes/reopens a browser page. Existing-viewer recovery across publisher restart, actual network loss/reconnect, remote receivers, TURN paths and broader browsers remain unqualified.
Physical Xorg/Wayland/portals, live HDMI picture/audio, hot unplug/replug, suspend/resume and Raspberry Pi remain unqualified.
The earlier first-save external-output URL failure is still unexplained. WebRTC settings and repeated UDP successes do not erase it; see linux-arm-robustness.json.
No new hardware encoder, amd64, Windows/macOS or full parity qualification. Ubuntu 24.04 coverage is an owned userland on the same Jetson/kernel.
hostChanges: No desktop/audio service restart, driver replacement or host package installation. Browser tools and Ubuntu container dependencies are user-owned fixtures.
